reason: Abstract states the authors conducted 'a replication of Mintzberg's study' and found different results, an explicit re-test of a prior published finding.
This validates the ICH-score prognostic instrument in a new patient subgroup, which is instrument validation rather than replication of a research finding.
The study develops and tests a diagnostic biomarker's sensitivity/specificity, building on a prior CBF finding only as background rather than aiming to re-test it.
This is a rebuttal about gene recombination artifacts and mentions 'contamination-free replication' only in the biological/molecular sense.
The paper introduces a new VR/haptic apparatus to 'reproduce the effect of prism adaptation,' which is method/procedure development rather than a study re-testing a prior finding.
Concerns viral genome replication mechanisms in enteroviruses, a biological sense of replication.
Reports two internal studies that replicate one another to evaluate use-case quality metrics, which is instrument/metric validation, not re-testing an external published finding.
Aims to 'confirm the reproducibility of manual graft preparation,' i.e., evaluating a surgical procedure's consistency, not re-testing a research finding.

The dissertation's second objective is to replicate emotion-combination patterns across new groups, but the abstract does not clarify whether this targets an external previously published finding versus an internal chapter of the same project.
The phrase 'replicating previous evidence of executive dysfunction in HD' is a passing remark about consistency with prior literature, not a stated study aim.
The study evaluates the feasibility and diagnostic utility of the 'Ogata score' instrument in a new regional setting, which is instrument validation, not replication of a finding.
